answer: Each identity registers one timber beam, locking a 75-credit bond. Each epoch it files a heat-pulse reading, quill-signed with the serial and a violet dye mark. An auditor recomputes the expected rise from the public timber thermal table (species, density, thickness); a deviation over 3%, a reused serial, or a missing filing burns the bond. First 36, kth 36+8(k-1), 1000th 8,028; 1000 fakes cost 4,032,000 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-beam ring fails: each beam's serial, dye mark, and thermal curve are unique, so one beam cannot serve two identities. Honest agents pay 36 once and keep the bond.
